agree.reason: For a household that felt the farm went quiet, a plain apology, a promised weekly email and a written credit rule that fits their exact complaint should move many of them to sign up, though nothing makes up for last year's lost $540.

honest.reason: Every fact traces to what the farmer supplied, but 'you'll get credit' in the closing hedge drops the more-than-a-third threshold, and 'many of you' stands in for 29 of 41 respondents.

works_the_facts.reason: Figures are restated rather than worked: it never says 29 of 41 respondents, and it never gives the credit per week (about $24.50 of $540 over 22 weeks) or what six half-weeks cost a member last year.

right_comparison.reason: It sets last year's handling (no credit, one email) against this year's rules at the same $540, which is the comparison that matters, but it never shows what the reader faces by staying out or by waiting while the 52 shares fill.

qualification.reason: The hedge is specific and checkable (a one-third cut triggers a week's credit, a Thursday email, nets only on tomatoes and peppers), though the 'if it happens' line weakens the threshold.

objections.reason: It meets 'you went quiet and kept our money' head-on with an apology, weekly emails and a credit rule, and admits loss can recur, but it leaves the reader's possible question about last year's lost value unanswered.

fit.reason: It is a short, warm email of about 180 words with a subject line, sign-off, deadline and link location, which matches the brief; it omits that pickup is still Thursdays.
